evidence.description: public nonisolated(unsafe) static let shared = EcosiaAuthWindowRegistry()

candidates.explanation: The use of `nonisolated(unsafe)` on the shared singleton instance bypasses Swift's compile-time concurrency safety checks. While the class uses a private queue for internal synchronization, this attribute signals that the instance is not thread-safe, which can lead to undefined behavior if accessed in ways that violate the internal synchronization logic.
candidates.title: Use of nonisolated(unsafe) on shared instance

evidence.description: public func registerWindow(_ windowUUID: WindowUUID) { queue.async(flags: .barrier) { [weak self] in self?._windows.insert(windowUUID) } EcosiaLogger.auth.info("Registered window: \(windowUUID)") }

public func unregisterWindow(_ windowUUID: WindowUUID) { queue.async(flags: .barrier) { [weak self] in self?._windows.remove(windowUUID) } EcosiaLogger.auth.info("Unregistered window: \(windowUUID)") }
public func clearAllWindows() { queue.async(flags: .barrier) { [weak self] in self?._windows.removeAll() } EcosiaLogger.auth.info("Cleared all windows") }

candidates.explanation: The `registerWindow`, `unregisterWindow`, and `clearAllWindows` methods perform asynchronous writes to the internal state but log the result synchronously. This creates a race condition where the log message may appear before the actual state change is committed to the `_windows` set, or the log might occur even if the `self` reference is nil inside the closure.
candidates.title: Race condition between asynchronous state updates and synchronous logging
